Deḥi is prepositive, so its position does not necessarily show which syllable of its chanted word has the stress. A stress helper shows it: a second deḥi on the first letter of the stressed syllable. MAM's template מ:דחי gives a chanted word in two forms, parameter 1 without the helper and parameter 2 with it, and since 2026-10-26 MAM-with-doc has shown parameter 2. Taamey D, the font of these pages, draws the helper as a top meteg, a vertical bar above its letter.

Below are the chanted words whose parameter 1 has a meteg on the letter where parameter 2 has the helper, the two parameters being otherwise the same. MAM's parameter 2 lacks that meteg, but with the helper drawn above the letter and the meteg below it, MAM-with-doc keeps the meteg: since 2026-10-27 it has shown each of these chanted words as parameter 2 with parameter 1's meteg. In each row, parameter 1 is above the chanted word as MAM-with-doc shows it, with both the meteg and the helper, and to their left is MAM's documentation note on the word, as MAM-with-doc shows it too. Each of those notes describes the meteg as “קו של געיה להורות על מקום הטעם”, a ga'ya stroke to show where the stress is.

A button above each note shows an English translation of the note in its place. These are AI-generated translations, not yet reviewed by a human: Claude, an AI model, translated the notes into English on 2026-10-27.

A meteg in parameter 1 is usually before the stressed syllable. Of MAM's 2,317 uses of מ:דחי, parameter 1 has no meteg in 2,053. In 255, it has meteg marks only before the stressed syllable. In 161 of those, a meteg is on an earlier atom of a maqaf compound, as in this chanted word from Ps3:7, shown with parameter 1 above parameter 2:

לֹֽא־אִ֭ירָא
לֹֽא־אִ֭ירָ֭א

In the other 94, the meteg marks are only earlier in the atom with the stress, as in this chanted word from Ps2:3:

נְֽ֭נַתְּקָה
נְֽ֭נַתְּקָ֭ה

Only in the 9 below is a meteg on the letter where parameter 2 has the helper.
